name: Vitamin C (topical)
lead: Topical vitamin C, most often as L-ascorbic acid, is used in serums intended to brighten the complexion, fade dark spots and provide antioxidant protection against environmental damage. It is among the best-known cosmeceuticals, popular alongside sunscreen in morning routines.

Studies suggest benefits for photoaging and hyperpigmentation, but trials are often small, sometimes industry-funded, and effectiveness is highly dependent on formulation, pH, concentration and stability.

paras: Ascorbic acid neutralizes free radicals generated by ultraviolet exposure, is a required cofactor for enzymes that stabilize collagen, and inhibits tyrosinase to reduce melanin production. It also helps regenerate vitamin E in skin. Skin penetration requires an acidic, adequately concentrated formulation.

L-ascorbic acid oxidizes easily, turning serums yellow or brown and reducing potency. Stinging and irritation can occur, particularly with low-pH products. It is not a substitute for sunscreen and is sold over the counter.
